input.body:
Owner decision 7 of #768, and the plan's explicit one-change constraint: **fetching and `migrationActive()` move onto versions in the same commit**. Splitting them would leave a version-gated fetch beside a date-windowed tolerance, which flags legacy shapes on repos that simply have not updated yet.

## The rule

A record declares the **version of its owning flow at which its change takes effect**, and lands in the same change as that bump. Which flow that is stays *structural* — read off where the record lives — so no record can declare the wrong one, and one field (`version`) serves engine and pack records alike.

A record applies while a repo sits **below** that number:

| repo state | what it fetches |
|---|---|
| up to date | nothing |
| lagging | exactly its gap — **however old those records are** |
| no stamp for that flow | the landed-date window, exactly as before |

The middle row is the part the date window structurally could not express: a dormant member was previously served only by the canon clone, because everything in its gap had aged out of the mount. The last row is "unknown is a state of its own" — a fresh adoption, a repo that has not converged since versions existed, and the canon itself, which is nobody's member and carries no stamp. Unknown is answered as unknown, never as version zero, which would make every record apply to everything forever.

`migrationApplies` is the single predicate behind both fetching and tolerance, so what a mount receives and what a check tolerates cannot mean different things. In a member the tolerance question reduces to "is the record in my mount" — the gate that put it there is the gate that tolerates it.

## The one constraint this buys

`version` must be a plain integer literal on its own line, because the version is read out of the record's *source* rather than by importing the spec — every caller is synchronous (`migrationActive` runs inside check bodies, and making it async would ripple through every rule in the corpus). A test imports every real record and asserts the two readings agree, so the constraint cannot rot silently.

## Blast radius

Exactly one live consumer of `migrationActive` today — `chrome-extension-release`'s `release-workflows`, keyed on a record from 2026-07-13 whose window closed weeks ago, so its answer was already `false` everywhere and stays `false`. All eleven existing records are stamped `version: 1`, so any repo already stamped at engine 1 fetches none of them: correct, because the applier runs unconditionally from the canon clone, so a stamped version implies those records were applied on the converge that stamped it.

## Verification

Beyond 1472 green tests, `selftest --strict`, clean work checks and an advisory list identical to `origin/main`, the gate was exercised against three real converges of a scratch member:

- **no stamp** → the two in-window records, exactly as before;
- **stamped engine 1 / packs 1** → no records at all;
- **rolled back to engine 0, packs cleared** → all five engine records ship including ones from July, while the pack records fall back to the date window because that flow's number is now unknown.

The writer test was watched failing without the wiring that hands the target's own stamp to the set.

Refs #768

input.body:
Rollout plan for the versioned-updates design (`docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md`, PR #767). Each phase is independently landable and leaves the fleet working; baselining keeps running until Phase 5 removes it.

## Phase 0 — Version scaffolding (no behavior change) — landed in #769
- [x] Give the engine a version: a `VERSION` (or equivalent) stamped into the mount by the vendor set, advanced by release.
- [x] Give each canon pack a version number in its manifest.
- [x] Add `min_engine_version` to the pack manifest schema; validate shape only (no enforcement yet). *(landed as `minEngineVersion` — manifest vocabulary is camelCase; owner confirmed 2026-08-12)*
- [x] Extend the member stamp (`.claudinite-checks.json`) to record installed engine version and per-pack versions alongside the existing fields. The date stamp stays authoritative for now.
- [x] Move each existing migration record into its owning flow's home: engine migrations to the engine's `migrations/`, pack migrations to `packs/<pack>/migrations/`. The flat canon-wide `migrations/` directory retires with the split (DESIGN §3.7, owner decision 8).
- [x] Instrument `escalation()` so the fired `code` is countable across the fleet (dispatch issues already carry it; make it aggregatable). This validates the cost model before Phase 2 (DESIGN §7).

## Phase 1 — Engine releases and the engine update flow
- [x] Define an engine release: a tagged snapshot that has passed the live canary rehearsal once, at release time. *(owner decision 2026-08-12: a release is the **bump commit**, canary-gated — no tag; `engine/RELEASES.md` + the `engine-release-record` check, #776)*
- [ ] Build the engine updater: clone the release's engine files into the mount wholesale, run engine migrations (version-ranged, regex-first, rarely code — **no `agentic:` field permitted on an engine migration**; enforce in the registry validator), converge the non-workflow wiring surfaces.
- [x] **Version-gate migration fetching in the vendoring flow** (owner decision 7): `compute-vendor-set` ships only the migration records above the repo's installed engine version, replacing the date-based recency window (`recordDirIsRecent`) as the fetch predicate. An up-to-date repo vendors none; a lagging repo vendors exactly its gap. *(#778)*
- [x] Rework `migrationActive()` legacy tolerance to be version-based in the same move ("tolerate the legacy shape while installed version < N") — it currently shares the recency window with fetching, and a version-gated fetch without this would flag legacy shapes on repos that simply haven't updated yet. *(#778 — same commit, as the constraint requires)*
- [ ] Gate auto-merge on `selftest --strict` of the converged tree; red → PR stays open + `need-human` label.
- [ ] Add the `force-merge-on-red-ci` per-invocation override (never a stored default).
- [ ] Define the **custom update** lane for the rare engine change that must touch `.github/workflows/` (MCP-credentialed session or human; explicitly named, never implicit).
- [ ] Move the `local-pack-namespace` declaration rewrite (bare id → `local/<id>`) into a real engine migration — it is a regex on the declaration file, and it closes the long-open "unimplemented normalization" gap (baselining task.md §3).

**Settled while building the gate** (#778), so later phases inherit it rather than re-deciding it:
- A record declares `version` — the owning flow's version its change takes effect at — and lands with that bump. Which flow owns it stays structural (where the record lives), so one field serves engine and pack records alike and none can name the wrong flow.
- `migrationApplies` is the single predicate behind fetching *and* tolerance. In a member, "is this tolerated" reduces to "is it in my mount".
- Unknown installed version → the landed-date window, unchanged. That covers a fresh adoption, a repo that has not converged since versions existed, and the canon itself, which carries no stamp.
- Phase 2's per-pack gate is the same function with the pack's number; nothing new to build for it.

## Phase 2 — Pack update flow
- [ ] Build the pack updater: vendor the new pack version, run its version-ranged migrations in order, converge wiring — **including `.github/workflows/`** (owner decision: workflow churn is the pack flow's; it lands through the MCP lane that baselining §2b uses today, which retires the withholding pattern).
- [ ] Apply the same version gate to per-pack migration fetching: only the records above the repo's installed version of *that pack* ship in the mount. *(the predicate already does this — what remains is the pack updater reading it)*
- [ ] Enforce `min_engine_version` before apply; violation → `need-human` terminal, never a guess.
- [ ] Implement the agentic apply stage: "apply the new pack rules — fix the repo, repair the tests," scoped to the update PR's branch.
- [ ] Re-home the executor-routine verification into this stage (the CCR routine is invisible to Actions; this is the only agent lane left).
- [ ] Uniform terminals: green → auto-merge per the repo's delivery setting; **any** non-green end (unanswered interview, red checks after repair, incomplete migration) → PR open + `need-human` + stop.

## Phase 3 — Install
- [ ] Install = the Phase 2 updater from a blank slate, **running no migrations** (owner decision 9): the vendored pack content is already the newest shape, so there is no older state to migrate — replaying history onto a fresh install is wasted work and a correctness hazard (migrations assume the shapes their era produced, not an empty repo). The install fetches no migration records and stamps the pack's **latest** version directly.
- [ ] Add run-once-at-install seed ops (the "initial op": plain code the runner executes once — not a version migration). Mark them so no later update re-runs them; the seeded-vs-converged distinction is load-bearing (README badge row is the precedent).
- [ ] Route the adoption interview through the open-PR + `need-human` terminal; converge `adopt-pack` / `adopt-claudinite` onto this runner.

## Phase 4 — Cutover
- [ ] Convert any remaining record semantics: the three `agentic:` notes → their owning pack's apply stage (or retire where already drained fleet-wide).
- [ ] Switch stamp authority from the date to installed versions; retire the held-stamp gating (#329/#330 semantics). *(fetching and tolerance already run on versions — what remains is note SELECTION)*

## Phase 5 — Retirement
- [ ] Remove `packs/basics/tasks/baselining/` (task.md, task.mjs, worker.mjs), its escalation codes, and its dispatch protocol, once every fleet member has updated through the new flows.
- [ ] Delete the `migrations/apply.mjs` + `migrations/registry.mjs` compatibility entry points (#769) — they exist only while a member's vendored worker can still invoke the old path.
- [ ] Drop the `agentic:` field from the migration schema.
- [ ] Vocabulary sweep: *baseline/baselining/rebaselining* → *update* across engine, packs, skills, docs (per `repo-text-sweeps`); rename the `adopt-claudinite` skill's baselining language; update sheepdog's `fleet-baseline` task name or note the exception.

## Ordering constraints
- Phase 1 before Phase 2: pack `min_engine_version` enforcement needs engine versions to exist; the version-gate + `migrationActive()` rework lands once, engine-side, and Phase 2 reuses it per pack.
- Phase 5 last, and only after fleet-wide adoption is verified (a member still on baselining must not lose its update path).
- The escalation-code measurement (Phase 0) should be read before committing Phase 2's scope — if `checks-not-green` dominates in practice, the agentic apply stage's budget deserves sizing to match.

## Risks
- **Skew during rollout**: while both mechanisms exist, a repo must be served by exactly one; gate by a per-repo flag in `.claudinite-checks.json`, flipped by the update that migrates it.
- **The regex-only discipline is a constraint on engine evolution**, accepted explicitly (DESIGN §2.3): a contract change that can't ship mechanically keeps backward compatibility or waits. Watch for pressure to route around it via "custom updates" — that lane is for workflows, not for contract changes.
- **Seed-op re-runs**: an install op that re-runs on update rewrites repo-owned surfaces (the README-diff class of bug). The run-once marking needs a conformance check of its own.
- **Tolerance/fetch coupling**: the version-gate must move fetching and `migrationActive()` together (one Phase 1 change, not two) — splitting them breaks legacy tolerance on lagging repos. *(done together in #778)*

content.text:
[#776](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/776) is merged (`140e89e`), main synced, conversation captured. Phase 1's next two boxes are done in a new PR.

**[#778](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/778) — the version gate**, fetching and tolerance moved together as the plan's constraint requires. CI is running.

A record now declares the version of its owning flow at which its change takes effect, and applies while a repo sits *below* that number:

| repo state | fetches |
|---|---|
| up to date | nothing |
| lagging | exactly its gap — however old those records are |
| no stamp for that flow | the landed-date window, exactly as before |

The middle row is what the date window structurally couldn't do: a dormant member used to be served only by the canon clone, because everything in its gap had aged out of the mount. `migrationApplies` is the single predicate behind both fetching and tolerance, so in a member "is this tolerated" reduces to "is it in my mount" — the gate that put it there is the gate that tolerates it.

Verified on three real converges of a scratch member — unstamped gets the two in-window records, stamped-at-1 gets none, rolled back to engine 0 gets all five engine records including July's. The writer test was watched failing without the wiring that hands the target's stamp to the set.

Blast radius is nil today: one live `migrationActive` consumer, keyed on a record whose window closed weeks ago.

Phase 2's per-pack gate now needs no new mechanism — it's the same function with the pack's number, which I've recorded on the issue so it isn't re-derived later.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#778](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/778) awaiting CI and your review. Next unbuilt box is the engine updater itself — the first one that changes how a member actually converges, so I'd want your read on the PR before starting it.
